walkthroughs.body_html:
Germany 1919-45 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Germany 1919-45 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Germany 1919-45.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who was murdered with Liebknecht in January 1919?
options: Eisner
Luxemburg
Ebert
Bebel

mcqs.q: What did the Wannsee Conference coordinate?
options: Operation Barbarossa
Final Solution
Munich Putsch
Enabling Act

mcqs.q: Why was the Weimar Republic politically unstable?
options: Proportional representation produced fragile coalitions; Article 48 enabled rule by decree; the 'stab-in-the-back' myth delegitimised the republic; extremists attacked from both left and right.
Weimar was unstable because Germans had never experienced democracy before.
Weimar was unstable because the Kaiser was still secretly in charge.
Because Germany was not invited to sign it.

mcqs.q: Why was the Berlin Wall built in 1961?
options: The Berlin Wall was built to stop a Western invasion of East Berlin.
Weimar was unstable because the Kaiser was still secretly in charge.
To stop the mass flow of East Germans to the West via Berlin (millions had fled), which was draining the GDR of skilled workers and threatening the regime's survival.
The Berlin Wall was built by NATO to keep East Germans out of West Germany.

mcqs.q: Why did the Treaty of Versailles cause resentment in Germany?
options: Because Germany was not invited to sign it.
Weimar was unstable because the Kaiser was still secretly in charge.
It assigned sole war guilt to Germany (Article 231) and imposed harsh reparations, territorial losses and military restrictions.
Because Germany lost more soldiers than any other country in the war.
